findings.claim: The new filter `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` does not do what its remarks say. A diagnostic built from a metadata member gets a null location, which becomes `Location.None`. `Location.None.IsInSource` is false, so `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource` is true and the diagnostic is reported. The only diagnostics dropped are those located in another compilation's syntax tree. So once the crash is fixed, a referenced closed generic struct whose public member lacks `[Key]` raises a location-less MsgPack004 Error in the consuming assembly. Ledger L8 says types from a referenced assembly are not analysed by the consumer, so this is a spurious build error, where before the change there was only an AD0001 warning. The same applies to MsgPack003-style `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull`, which now gets a null location from `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericStructDiagnosticFilterTests.MetadataMemberMissingKey_IsNotReportedInConsumingCompilation. `lib` is emitted in memory with `[MessagePackObject] struct Item<T>`, which has a public property without `[Key]`. `app` uses `Item<int>`. On head the verifier reports an unexpected MsgPack004 with no location.

findings.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` indexes: lines 735, 1009 and 1101 in the reporter's version. The diff fixes only the two that map to 982 and 1074, an offset of -27. Applying the same offset, the third site is around line 708 of GetObjectInfo. No hunk touches it, so it presumably still indexes `[0]`. It can still throw IndexOutOfRangeException (CS8785/AD0001) for a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly whenever that diagnostic path is taken.

receipt_plan.detail: Grep head TypeCollector.cs for `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. Any remaining hit inside GetObjectInfo (near line 708) is reachable for metadata symbols through CollectGeneric's closed-generic branch.
